_comment: HOSTING: all four archives are now served from the realm's own VPS at http://152.53.115.249/patches/ instead of GitHub releases. URLs are IMMUTABLE and carry the version in the filename -- the bytes behind a URL never change, so a player who started a download an hour ago can resume it safely, and rolling back is repointing at the previous filename (which is still on disk). The path field is what lands in the client and never carries a version: load order depends only on the archive letter. To publish a new version see PUBLISHING-PATCHES.md.
_comment2: MIRRORS: M and N are Trimitor's work and are NOT forked -- these are byte-identical copies of his release assets, still pinned to his tags, served from our host so that a deleted release or a dead repo cannot break new installs. The upstream each one came from is recorded in /srv/uncapped-patches/mirrors.tsv on the VPS, and a daily systemd timer (uncapped-mirror-check) reports when upstream ships a newer release carrying the same asset, or replaces the asset behind our pinned tag. Re-mirroring is always a deliberate act.

_letter: U, not R. It has to sort after every archive it replaces -- and -S sorted AFTER -R. Every haste tooltip therefore described a mechanic that does not exist here -- report #259 (Warrior Flurry) is the visible half. 126 spells / 171 Description+ToolTip fields relabelled, selected by AURA TYPE (the ten types the diverting handlers serve: 9, 65, 138, 140, 141, 192, 193, 216, 218, 252) intersected with player reachability (SkillLineAbility + Talent + SpellItemEnchantment + item_template.spellid_*, closed over EffectTriggerSpell), then extended by hand with the talent/glyph/summon rows whose TEXT quotes one of those auras ($8515s1% melee haste). ⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED, and each for a reason that is about the code not the wording: negative amounts (Thunder Clap, Curse of Tongues, Icy Touch, Frost Fever, Hurricane) still slow exactly as written; PET haste (Cobra Reflexes, Frenzy, Ghoul Frenzy) is real because a pet is a Creature and the IsPlayer() guard fails; creature enrages likewise; amounts >= 1000 hit SetInstantCast and return BEFORE the diversion; and haste RATING is diverted at a DIFFERENT rate (1000 rating = +1% crit damage, in Player::ApplyRatingMod), so hundreds of item/enchant/food tooltips still say 'haste rating' and need a separate decision. _history6: 2026-08.08c: Spell.dbc -- the SAME 565 custom mounts can now be cast while moving. Cast-while-moving is a shipped realm feature with two halves that have to agree. The SERVER half (src/server/scripts/Custom/cast_while_moving.cpp:101) strips SPELL_INTERRUPT_FLAG_MOVEMENT (0x01, SpellDefines.h:26) from every cast-time spell at startup and the live log confirms it runs: 'Cast while moving: cleared movement interrupt on 13936 cast-time spell(s)'. The CLIENT half is this Spell.dbc, and it has to carry the same stripped flags because the client refuses the cast locally and never sends a packet -- which is why no server change could ever reach this. The 565 custom mount rows were authored separately and never went through the stripping pass. Report #292 ('you cannot mount the starter dog mount while moving, like every other mount') is the visible half via starter mount 850139. MEASURED, and this doubles as the proof that field 31 is InterruptFlags since no other field gives this answer: spells game-wide still carrying 0x01 = 565, and they are EXACTLY ids 850000-850564, with 0 anywhere else in the game. DISTRIBUTION: all 565 read 31 (0x1F) uniformly -- MOVEMENT|PUSH_BACK|INTERRUPT|AUTOATTACK|DAMAGE -- and all 565 become 30 (0x1E). The bit was MASKED OFF, not assigned: assigning 30 happens to agree today, but the other four bits are real and had to survive, and a future row that read something other than 31 would have been silently flattened. 30 is exactly what stock Brown Horse (458) and Golden Gryphon (32235) carry, so the 565 end up flag-identical to real Blizzard mounts rather than to a value we invented. BLAST RADIUS, measured by diffing the record block against 08.08b: 565 differing bytes, 565 rows, ONE distinct field touched (31), spell ids touched == exactly 850000..850564, string block byte-identical, record/field counts unchanged. Game-wide carriers of 0x01 afterwards: 0. Negative controls: Fireball 133, Heal 2054, Shadow Bolt 686, Wrath 5176 all keep 14 (0x0E) unchanged; Brown Horse 458 and Golden Gryphon 32235 keep 30; custom-but-not-a-mount Mending Fatigue 850565 keeps 0; fabricated filenames absent. Built by ADDING to 08.08b, never repacked -- the 08.08b SkillLineAbility.dbc survives byte-identical (sha256 3d3cd188589666a0..., all 565 SkillLine-777 rows still readable out of 08.08c). verify-stack with M= and N= in BOTH stacks, 08.08b -> 08.08c: 5758 reachable both sides, 0 lost, 0 newly reachable, exactly 1 file CHANGED (Spell.dbc) which is the intent, other 13 DBCs byte-identical including skilllineability.dbc. NOTE the archive grew 16.1MB -> 20.6MB: replacing the 49.5MB Spell.dbc does not reclaim its old block. Content is correct; compacting stays a separate, deliberate change. WHY IT IS SAFE TO DO AT ALL: the six keys were never a set to complete -- every postbox independently summons three Undead Postmen and then Postmaster Malown eight seconds later (smart_scripts on 176346/176349/176350/176351/176352/176353), so any ONE key already got you the boss and the other five were redundant doors to the same encounter. _history9: 2026-08.17a: Spell.dbc CHANGED and ItemExtendedCost.dbc ADDED (new to this archive). Seven Spell.dbc edits, each the client half of a server change in the same build, plus one regression fix for a bug WE shipped on 08.16a. ★★ THE BASE WAS THE PUBLISHED 08.16a ARCHIVE (sha aa0cfbbceaeb..., the file pinned here before this line was rewritten), extracted with mpqlib -- NOT Launcher/work/Spell.dbc and NOT Spell.published.dbc, both of which predate the 08.08a haste->crit-damage rewrite and/or the 08.16a Moonkin block, and either would have silently reverted live fixes invisibly until a player read a tooltip. ⚠ THE REGRESSION FIRST, because it is why the rest is safe to apply: #880r, 16 rows (Healing Touch x15 + Nourish 50464), AttributesEx2 |= ALLOW_WHILE_NOT_SHAPESHIFTED. 08.16a set Stances non-zero on 47 druid heals to allow Moonkin healing; Rejuvenation/Regrowth/Lifebloom/Swiftmend already carried 0x00080000, but Healing Touch and Nourish did not -- their stock Stances of 0 was the ONLY thing making them legal out of form. Making Stances non-zero without granting the attribute pushed CheckShapeshift into its final else branch, so every druid on the realm in plain caster form was told to shapeshift first to cast their own basic heal, for two days. BLOCKING pair (the server change is a complete NO-OP without the client half, because the client refuses the cast locally and never sends a packet): #703 Cat Swipe 62078, frontal chain -> 360-degree self-centred AoE -- TargetA=18, TargetB=16, Radius=14, ChainTarget=0, Facing=0, all five read straight off Fan of Knives 51723 (the only other spell that is both self-centred-area AND WEAPON_PERCENT_DAMAGE), so Swipe is made field-identical to a shipping Blizzard spell rather than to invented numbers; and #923, the same 47 druid heal rows, Stances |= FORM_CAT (bit 0 -- forms are 1-indexed, the bit is form-1) and StancesNot &= ~FORM_CAT. ItemExtendedCost.dbc is the client half of #834 (arena personal/team rating requirement dropped from 162 rows); the server half is the itemextendedcost_dbc table, and shipping only one side leaves the client drawing a rating requirement the server no longer enforces. _comment: THE PATCHED CLIENT EXECUTABLE. Stock 3.3.5a 12340 with LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE set and an import-table entry for UncappedCT.dll, which is what gets our code loaded before the client's entry point runs. Shipped whole rather than patched on the player's machine: every install then runs a byte-identical binary we can verify by hash, instead of the output of patch logic running on 40 different machines. The path is the RENAMED name the launcher's client hardening uses -- ClientHardening deletes a stock Wow.exe when this file is present, so the install ends up with exactly one runnable client.
_note: Not in payload/ and never committed: it is a modified Blizzard binary, and the payload tree is a public git repo.

_comment: THE INJECTED RUNTIME. A HARD dependency of the executable above -- import injection means the loader resolves it before any game code runs, so if this file is missing the client does not start at all (exit 0xC0000135, STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND). The launcher checks for it before every launch and tells the player to add an antivirus exclusion, because a real-time scanner quarantining it AFTER the sync verified it is the realistic way it goes missing. Built /MT so KERNEL32 is its only import: a 3.3.5a install has no reason to have a VC redistributable.
_note: Must stay in step with the executable above: they share the wire-magnitude codec and the native-channel frame format. Publish them together, always.
_history_0814a: 2026-08.14a: THE WIDENED FRAME DIAGNOSTIC. 13c shipped the once-a-second frame-time bucket line and it answered the first question (frames collapse with cooldown-query storms, not with pull size: 178 fps at ~5k queries/sec against 23 fps at ~150k, with FEWER units on screen). It could not answer the second -- WHOSE code -- so this build adds three things the investigation asked for: a stall watchdog that reads the Lua call stack while the client is actually frozen, a sampling profiler that takes 512 instruction-pointer samples per burst and counts where the time genuinely is, and a hooked FrameScript_SignalEvent counter. ⚠ THIS IS A WIDENING OF WHAT IS COLLECTED: the watchdog reports Lua chunk names and line numbers, so addon FILE PATHS now leave the player's machine where 13c sent only numbers. Chunks loaded from a string carry player text as their name and are reported as a bare token with the content dropped. Attestation is untouched -- spec 0x058B902B, 300 variants, identical to 13c, so this is not a variant-set change. ★ AND THE REAL LESSON OF THIS RELEASE IS NOT IN THE DLL: 13c's diagnostic was switched off less than a day later by an unrelated client bundle, because New-Manifest.ps1 defaulted fpsReportWebhook to '' and a release passes the flags it is thinking about. A null webhook does not pause collection, it deletes the logs. The generator now inherits both webhooks when the flag is absent.
_history_0809b: 2026-08.09b: CLIENT ATTESTATION. The DLL now answers a server challenge on opcode 0x513 (topic ATT) that an addon-only client cannot even receive, because 0x513 dispatches through a table only the DLL registers into. 300 generated response variants, regenerated per release. ⚠ THE INTERLOCK IS THE IMPORTANT PART: the DLL carries a plain-text marker (UNCAPPED-ATTEST-SPEC:...) and tools/attestation/check_release.py is wired into New-Manifest.ps1, which THROWS before writing the manifest if the DLL, the generated .inc, this pin and the bytes actually served do not all agree. Server and client must hold the same variant set or every player fails at once. ★ ALSO CARRIES 2026-08.09a, which was published to the host at 01:03 on 2026-08-09 and NEVER PINNED -- it sat served and unreferenced while every player kept running 08.07b. Reconstructed the pre-attestation source and diffed it against the published 09a: 6 differing bytes, both copies of the PE timestamp, so the working tree IS 09a's source and its content is carried forward here. What 09a changed versus 07b could not be determined -- ~1.4KB of .text across Hook_ItemCount/DecodeWireMagnitude/DllMain/DsRead/EnsureNetHandler, no size, string or import change, and kVaultAwareReturns byte-identical in both, so it is NOT another vault-return edit. That unpinned-DLL gap is why Launcher/tools/preflight-release.sh now exists.
_history: 2026-08.07b: hooks 0x005E2797 + 0x005E27B0, the QUEST LOG / TRACKER objective text -- "Akiris Reed: 0/10" on the mob tooltip while the Vault held 4 (quest 617, item 4029). ★ THESE ARE THE TWO ADDRESSES 07a's note calls wrong and says were removed. They are not bad addresses; they were attached to the wrong bug. 07a was chasing the greyed questgiver button, inferred these from disassembly, shipped them, saw no change, and deleted them -- correctly, since they never fire at a questgiver. But deleting them threw away the fix for a different symptom nobody had reported yet. Now observed by the diagnostic with the symptom on screen: 'UNHOOKED site ret=005E2797 item=4029 bags=0 vault=4' and the same for 005E27B0, two adjacent sites in one tick as the objective text builds have-vs-need.
